title: How a cache serves a request
summary: A conceptual cache-aside lookup: a hit returns stored data; a miss loads the data and fills the cache for the next request. Freshness and eviction are separate flows.

nodes.name: Request data
nodes.description: A caller asks for a value by its key.

nodes.name: Look up the key
nodes.description: The cache checks whether it already holds the requested value.

nodes.name: Return cached value
nodes.description: The caller receives the cached value without loading it again.

nodes.name: Load the value
nodes.description: On a miss, the application fetches the value from its original source.

nodes.name: Fill the cache
nodes.description: The application stores the loaded value for future requests.

nodes.name: Return loaded value
nodes.description: The caller receives the value loaded from the source.

nodes.name: Cache hit
nodes.description: The key has a cached value, so the caller can use it immediately.

nodes.name: Cache miss
nodes.description: The key has no cached value, so the application must load it.

next_flow: Expiration, invalidation, and eviction decide when cached data stops being usable.
